chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang vs the Office — Thumb-Sized Buddhas & Shadow Binding
chapter_meta_description: Invisible Li Huowang fights a swarm of thumb-sized golden Buddhas, breaks his own ribs for shared pain, and faces a brush that erases him from reality. Peng Longteng arrives.
og_title: Manifestation — A Desperate Heist in the Shadows
og_description: Li Huowang’s invisibility fails, his weapons shatter, and a Daoist’s brush begins erasing him. Only pain and a headless corpse can save him now.
twitter_title: Thumb Buddhas & Shadow Binding — Li Huowang vs the Office
twitter_description: Li Huowang crushes golden Buddhas underfoot and jams ribs into his chest to fight a full Office squad. Peng Longteng appears where she shouldn’t be.

lore_anchors.definition: A sword made from the bone of a powerful being; this one is Zhuge Yuan’s remains, carrying his lingering warmth and emotional weight.
The headless female corpse of a convict-soldier general from Siqi; she serves as Li Huowang’s supernatural summon.

A miniature golden Buddha-entity that emerges from a person’s body; it can speak in unison, cast mind-control suggestions (like “lay down the butcher’s knife”), and physically block attacks with its head.
A government-sponsored supernatural law enforcement body that hunts rogue cults and prevents Heavenly Calamities; its agents are highly trained and equipped with specialized ritual tools.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does the Daoist’s brush turn the user’s hair gray?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Using the Kui Star Brush consumes the user’s life force or qi, visibly aging them with each stroke—a common trade-off in xianxia when wielding high-grade ritual tools.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why can’t Li Huowang just run away when his shadow is pinned?
cultural_notes_faq.a: His shadow is a reflection of his body’s yin-yang connection; pinning it freezes his physical movement, not just his shadow’s location—body and shadow are linked in Chinese folk magic.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What’s with the thumb-sized golden Buddhas?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They are miniature Buddha-emanations that can speak, move, and cast subtle mental influences; they represent a corrupted, parasitic form of Buddhist power in the Dao-Twisted World.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Peng Longteng’s appearance such a shock to the Daoist?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Kui Star Brush should suppress all summoned or supernatural entities; the fact that she appears despite the brush’s effect implies Li Huowang’s power operates on a different set of rules.
